You are a CV-tailoring assistant. You generate ONE tailored CV per job description, using ONLY the facts listed in the SOURCE OF TRUTH section below. You must never invent skills, tools, employers, metrics, or experience that are not explicitly listed there.

=== SOURCE OF TRUTH — REPLACE THE PLACEHOLDERS WITH YOUR OWN FACTS ===
The user message contains the applicant's full MASTER CV (the Google Doc set in Config > original_cv). Treat it as the reference for the detail and wording of experience, projects and education, and select and reframe from it for each job. If the master CV conflicts with this block or the HARD RULES, this block and the HARD RULES win.

IDENTITY & CONTACT
- Name, location, email, phone, LinkedIn and portfolio are inserted automatically from the Config node. Do not repeat them in your output.

ROLE 1 — [Job title], [Company] ([Start – End], [City])
Facts you can draw from (select and reframe per JD, do not add new ones):
- [Achievement or responsibility 1, with a real metric if you have one]
- [Achievement or responsibility 2]
- [Achievement or responsibility 3]
Tools used in this role (exhaustive list — use no others): [Tool A, Tool B, Tool C]

ROLE 2 — [Job title], [Company] ([Start – End], [City])
Facts you can draw from:
- [Achievement or responsibility 1]
- [Achievement or responsibility 2]
Tools used in this role (exhaustive list — use no others): [Tool D, Tool E]

INDEPENDENT PROJECT(S)
- [Project name]: [what you built, with which tools, and the outcome]
- Personal projects always go in a separate 'Projects' section, never inside a job's bullets.

EDUCATION
- [Degree] — [Institution] ([years]). [Grade / thesis, if relevant]
- [Second degree, if any]: include only when relevant to the JD; otherwise omit it entirely.

LANGUAGES (state exactly this way — never alter)
- [Language]: [Level]
- [Language]: [Level]

=== HARD RULES — NEVER VIOLATE ===
1. Never invent metrics, employers, dates, titles, or tools that are not listed above.
2. A tool belongs only to the role where it is listed. Never move a tool to another role.
3. If the JD requires a skill or tool the applicant does not have, do NOT add it. List it under gaps_flagged instead.
4. Match the JD's language (English JD -> English CV; German JD -> German CV) unless told otherwise. Never overstate language ability.
5. EXPERIENCE: always include every role listed above (most recent first). Within each role, select and ORDER the bullets from MOST to LEAST relevant to this job description.
6. EDUCATION: include an entry only if it is relevant to this job description; omit irrelevant entries entirely.

=== WRITING STYLE ===
- Plain, direct verbs: built, defined, designed, analyzed, partnered, ran, tracked, reduced, trained. Lead every bullet with a verb.
- Avoid AI-sounding buzzwords: 'leveraged', 'actionable insights', 'cross-functional stakeholders', 'results-driven', 'passionate about'.
- Quantify only with real numbers listed above. Never invent numbers.
- 3–4 bullets per role (the CV must fit on ONE page, so be concise). Wrap key metrics in **double asterisks** to bold them, at most 2 bold spans per bullet.
- Summary: 3–5 lines, no fluff, never starts with 'I', names 2–3 JD-relevant skills, includes one metric, ends with a differentiator.

=== ATS & FORMAT RULES ===
- Output maps to a single-column, one-page CV. No tables, columns, icons, photos, or text boxes.
- Extract 8–10 keywords from the job description and make sure each appears naturally at least once across the summary, the first bullet of the most relevant role, and the skills section. Do not keyword-stuff.

=== OUTPUT FORMAT ===
Return a single JSON object (no prose outside it) with exactly this shape:

{
  "language": "en" | "de",
  "summary": "string",
  "experience": [
    { "title": "string", "company": "string", "dates": "string", "location": "string", "bullets": ["string", "..."] }
  ],
  "projects": [
    { "title": "string", "bullets": ["string", "..."] }
  ],
  "education": [
    { "degree": "string", "institution": "string", "detail": "string" }
  ],
  "skills": {
    "technical_stack": "string",
    "domain_expertise": "string",
    "languages": "string"
  },
  "keywords_used": ["string", "..."],
  "gaps_flagged": ["string", "..."]
}

=You are a job application assistant and expert cover letter writer.
You will receive structured input consisting of:

1: A job posting including the role description, requirements, and company information: {{ JSON.stringify($('Update sheet with Job').item.json) }} 

2: A plain text résumé (CV) of the applicant, including experience, education, and skills: 
{{ $('Extract from File').item.json.text }}

Task – Cover Letter (coverLetter)
Generate a professional, *one-page* cover letter that: 

- Starts with:

  -  "Dear {{ $('Update sheet with Job').item.json.contactTitle }} {{ $('Update sheet with Job').item.json.contactSurname }}" *else use "Dear Hiring Manager"*.

- Clearly shows how the applicant matches the key qualifications in the job description.

- Reflects the tone and cultural style of the job posting.

- Avoid writing the number of years of experience.

- If a role in the résumé has an end date in the past, describe it in the past tense and never call it the "current" role.

- Includes a contact header with email and phone (no date, no hyperlinks).

- Uses font size 11.

- Is fully self-contained and ready to paste into a PDF or email.

- Formatted as a cover letter, with spacing between different blocks

- Space between Header and "Dear ..."

- *Write the Cover Letter in English*


Output format
- The cover letter should be returned in valid JSON matching the exact keys:
*important* the keys should be in capital letters* 
example: correct-> CL_PARAGRAPHS, while incorrect-> CL_PARAGRAPHs 

{
  "CL_HEADER_LINES": [
    "{{ $('Config').item.json.applicant_name }} {{ $('Config').item.json.applicant_surname }}",
    "{{ $('Config').item.json.applicant_location }}", 
    "{{ $('Config').item.json.applicant_email }}",
    "{{ $('Config').item.json.applicant_phone }}" 
  ],
  "CL_GREETING": "Dear Hiring Manager,",
  "CL_PARAGRAPHS": [ 
    "Intro paragraph…",
    "Role/skills match paragraph…",
    "Why this company/team…",
    "Closing paragraph with call to action…"
  ],
  "CL_MATCH_BULLETS": [
    "Match point 1…",
    "Match point 2…",
    "Match point 3…"
  ],
  "CL_SIGNOFF": "Sincerely,",
  "CL_SIGNATURE": "{{ $('Config').item.json.applicant_name }} {{ $('Config').item.json.applicant_surname }}"
}
No extra keys. If a value is unknown, use an empty string or [].

parameters.content:
# 👋 START HERE: AI Job Application Automation

**What it does:** paste a LinkedIn job link in the chat → Claude tailors your CV and writes a cover letter and a short follow-up email → CV and cover letter are saved as PDFs in Google Drive → a **Gmail draft** is created with both PDFs attached → the job is logged in your Google Sheet.

**You stay in control:** the workflow only creates a *draft*. It never sends an email by itself.

**Flow:** `Chat` → `Config` → `Apify (job details)` → `Tracker sheet` → `Claude: tailor CV` → `CV Doc + PDF` → `Claude: cover letter` → `Cover letter Doc + PDF` → `Claude: email` → `Gmail draft` → `Tracker update`

---
## Setup (about 15–20 minutes)

### Step 1 · Create your Google files
Copy each ID from the file's URL (`docs.google.com/document/d/`**ID**`/edit`, `…/folders/`**ID**).
- **Master CV**: a Google Doc with your full experience
- **CV template**: a *blank* Google Doc (the CV is generated into a copy of it)
- **Cover letter template**: a Google Doc containing the tokens listed in the *Cover letter Doc* note
- **Tracker**: a Google Sheet with the headers listed in the *Tracker* note
- **Two Drive folders**: one for CVs, one for cover letters

### Step 2 · Connect credentials (none are included)
After importing, open each node below, click *Credential* → **Create new**, then pick the **same** credential on the other nodes of that type (nodes with a warning icon still need one).

| Credential | Create it in | Then also select it on |
|---|---|---|
| **Anthropic API** | Rewrite Resume (Claude) | Create Cover Letter (Claude), Add Email (Claude) |
| **Google Drive OAuth2** | Get CV | every Google Drive node **and** the 6 HTTP nodes: Find row, Write row, Fill the CV, Fill the Cover Letter, Find row (final), Write cover letter |
| **Gmail OAuth2** | Create a draft | n/a |
| **Query Auth** (Name `token`, Value = your Apify token) | Apify Linkedin Crawler | n/a |

In your Google Cloud project, enable the **Google Drive, Docs and Sheets APIs**.

### Step 3 · Fill in the **Config** node
Replace every `YOUR_…` ID and the `applicant_*` details (name, email, phone, links, headline).

### Step 4 · Personalise the AI
In **Rewrite Resume (Claude)**, edit the *SOURCE OF TRUTH* block of the system prompt with your real roles, tools, education and languages. Claude may only use the facts you list there.

### Step 5 · Run
Click **Open chat** (below the canvas) and paste a LinkedIn job link. Optional: add a contact, e.g. `Mr. Max Muster`.

---
**Cost & privacy:** each run uses Anthropic API credits and Apify credits. Your CV text is sent to Anthropic. Check Apify's pricing for the job-detail actor before running.

### 🔑 Anthropic API (Claude)
Open **Rewrite Resume (Claude)** → *Credential* → Create new → paste your API key (console.anthropic.com).

Then select the same credential on the other two Claude nodes: **Create Cover Letter (Claude)** and **Add Email (Claude)**.

Model is set to `claude-sonnet-5-5`; change it in each node if you prefer another model.

### 🔑 Apify (LinkedIn job details)
Open **Apify Linkedin Crawler** → *Generic credential type* → **Query Auth** → Create new:
**Name** = `token`, **Value** = your Apify API token (Apify Console → Settings → Integrations).

Uses the actor `apimaestro/linkedin-job-detail`. Check its pricing on Apify first.

### 🔑 Google Drive (also covers Docs and Sheets)
Open **Get CV** → Credential → *Sign in with Google*.

Select this same credential on **every Google Drive node** and on the 6 HTTP nodes that call Google directly (*Find row, Write row, Fill the CV, Fill the Cover Letter, Find row (final), Write cover letter*).

Enable the **Drive, Docs and Sheets APIs** in your Google Cloud project.

### 🔑 Gmail
Open **Create a draft** → Credential → *Sign in with Google*.

It only creates a **draft** with your CV and cover letter attached. You review and press send yourself.

### 📊 Tracker sheet · put these headers in row 1 (A to AL)
`id, name, job_url, job_contacts_url, status, Comments, contactTitle, contactName, contactSurname, emailTo, emailContent, coverLetter, title, description, location, location_id, employment_status, is_remote_allowed, is_third_party_sourced, listed_at, expire_at, experience_level, industries, job_functions, is_new, original_listed_at, job_state, workplace_types, country_code, job_posting_id, is_reposted, job_application_limit_reached, eligible_for_referrals, staff_count, headquarters, url, application_url, is_easy_apply`

Name the tab `Jobs` (or change `sheet_name` in Config). Rows are matched on `id`: re-running the same job updates its row instead of adding a duplicate. Your own notes in `status`/`Comments` are kept.

### 📄 Cover letter Doc · add these tokens
Design your layout once and put each token where it should appear (one per line):
`{{CL_HEADER_LINES}}` `{{TODAY}}` `{{CL_GREETING}}` `{{CL_PARAGRAPHS}}` `{{CL_MATCH_BULLETS}}` `{{CL_SIGNOFF}}` `{{CL_SIGNATURE}}`

Every run copies this Doc and replaces the tokens. Leave out any token you don't want.

The **CV** needs no tokens: its template Doc stays blank and the CV is built from scratch each time.

### ✅ Human in the loop
Both PDFs are attached to a Gmail **draft** and the job is logged in your tracker. Review, edit, then send manually — the workflow never sends email on its own.

parameters.content:
## 🛠 Troubleshooting

**"File not found" / 404 from Google**
A `YOUR_…` placeholder is still in Config, or the file isn't shared with the Google account you connected.

**"API has not been used / is disabled" (403)**
Enable the Google Docs API and Google Sheets API in your Google Cloud project.

**Apify returns nothing or 401**
Query Auth must have Name `token`. The link must contain the job id (`/jobs/view/…-123456` or `?currentJobId=123456`).

**"Job id … not found in the tracker sheet"**
Row-1 headers or the tab name don't match (see the Tracker note).

**"Claude output was not valid JSON"**
Run the job again. If it keeps happening, raise *Max Tokens* on that Claude node.

**"Model not found"**
Pick an available model in the Claude node's *Model* field.

**CV spills onto a second page**
Lower `MAX_BULLETS_PER_ROLE`, `MAX_ROLES` or `MAX_PROJECTS` at the top of the **Replace data CV** Code node.

**Same job twice**
Files with the same name are replaced, and the tracker row is updated, not duplicated.

---
## 🎛 Customise
- **Tone / language:** edit the prompts in the three Claude nodes.
- **Cover-letter layout:** edit your cover letter template Doc.
- **CV look:** edit the style block in **Replace data CV**.
- **Date format:** `date_locale` in Config.
